notes: The tv2_unreal testbed's TObjectPtr handle resolution (docs 25.20/25.22): applied only through binding files (models/bindings), never by import name. Read from the binaries' code: rcx is the handle slot's address; the slot holds a resolved pointer, or an unresolved handle (low bit set) that a resolver reached through a global function pointer turns into the object's address, written back to the slot; the result is that address. Access tracking (LOCK-protected counters in a global table and the tracking calls) and the resolver's own work are library-private state (accessor-private-state).

entries.name: ResolveHandle
entries.notes: Development: the whole accessor (tracking inline, rva 0x4e10); DebugGame: the resolving half (rva 0xa970). Result: the resolved object, never on a stack (nonstack); the object is not where its handle lives within its first 0x400 bytes (result_separate_from_reads). The result row also reads rsp: the body keeps the value in stack spills on the way (an address input).

entries.name: TrackAccess
entries.notes: DebugGame: the access-tracking half (rva 0x9200), given the resolved pointer in rcx: private tracking state only; it changes no handle resolution (preserves ResolveHandle's accessor state).
